get.description: Versioned API root for v1. Returns basic service metadata useful for humans and automation: the service name, API version, runtime environment, and links to interactive docs and metrics when those features are enabled. Ideal for quick health inspection, service discovery, and integration tests.

A lightweight liveness endpoint that returns a plain 'ok' string. Designed for container orchestrators (Kubernetes, Nomad, etc.) to check that the application process is running. This endpoint performs no external network calls or expensive checks and should respond quickly.

A readiness endpoint that performs dependency checks and returns a JSON object describing the health of critical components (for example Memgraph and Redis). The response includes an aggregate status ('ok', 'degraded', or 'error'), a timestamp, and per-dependency details. Returns HTTP 200 when the service is ready or degraded (if a safe fallback is allowed), and HTTP 503 when not ready. This endpoint is intended for load balancers and deployment tooling to decide whether the instance should receive traffic.

A diagnostic startup endpoint intended for use during deployment and provisioning. It returns the same detailed JSON shape as /ready but is labeled as 'startup' to help operators distinguish pre-boot checks from runtime readiness. Use this endpoint to surface detailed dependency errors, migration state, and reasons an instance may not be ready to accept traffic.

post.summary: Obtain a JWT access token (OAuth2 Password Grant)
post.description: Issue a short-lived JWT access token using the OAuth2 Password Grant form flow. Clients must POST a form with 'username' and 'password' (and optional 'scope' as a space-delimited list). On success the endpoint returns a JSON object with 'access_token', 'token_type' (bearer), and 'expires_in' (seconds). This demo implementation accepts any non-empty credentials and issues tokens with the 'user' scope; in production replace the authenticator with a secure identity provider.

get.summary: Get current user claims from token
get.description: Return information extracted from the currently presented Bearer token. Clients must present the token in the Authorization header as 'Bearer <token>'. The response includes the token subject (username) and the granted scopes. This endpoint is useful for client-side UI to display the current user or for quick token inspection.

post.description: Create or initialize a stateful agent session. POST an `AgentRequest` to reserve a `session_id` that can be used for subsequent session operations. The server may return an existing session identifier if the client supplied `session_id`, otherwise it will mint a new one. Sessions are useful for long-running or interactive agent workflows where multiple steps or cancellations may occur.

get.description: List agent sessions with pagination.
List steps associated with a session with pagination.

post.summary: Send a step to a session
post.description: Advance a stateful agent session by sending a single step payload. The request body should be a `SessionStepRequest` containing an `input` object relevant to the session's next action. This can be used to supply new user messages, tool results, or other events the agent should process. The endpoint returns an acknowledgement; in full implementations it may return the updated session state or produced output.

get.description: Retrieve the current state of a previously created agent session. The response includes identifiers and a minimal status (for example `active`, `completed`, or `cancelled`). This demo implementation returns a simple stub; a real implementation would include the session's history, last step, and other metadata.

delete.description: Request cancellation of a stateful agent session. This signals the orchestrator to stop any ongoing work and mark the session as cancelled. Cancellation is best-effort; the endpoint returns an acknowledgement indicating the request was accepted. Subsequent calls to `GET /sessions/{session_id}` should reflect the cancelled state.

post.description: Start an agent execution. POST an `AgentRequest` to create a new run and receive an `AgentResponse`.

get.description: Discover and list available tools that the platform can dispatch to. This endpoint performs a best-effort scan of the `src.mcp.tools` package and returns a paginated list of detected tools with short names, import paths, and a detected entrypoint if present. If discovery fails or no tools are present, a small seed list is returned so clients have predictable values to display. Use pagination parameters `page_size` and `page_token` to traverse large inventories. The response includes `ETag` headers to support client-side caching and conditional requests.

schema.title: Response List Tools V1 Tools Get

post.summary: Invoke a tool by name (create invocation)
post.description: Invoke the named tool by its short dotted name (for example `graph.query`). The request body can be a `ToolInvokeRequest` containing `args` (a JSON object passed as keyword arguments to the tool) and an optional `timeout_seconds` to bound execution. Clients may supply an `Idempotency-Key` header to ask the server to cache and re-use previous results for identical requests. The endpoint returns structured provenance (trace_id/event_id) and timing information along with the tool result.

get.summary: Get tool metadata and input schema if available
get.description: Return best-effort metadata about a specific tool identified by its short name. The response contains the Python module import path, any detected callable entrypoint, a short description (from the module docstring), and an optional input schema if the tool exposes `INPUT_SCHEMA` or a `get_input_schema()` helper. This is useful for client UIs that want to render tool-specific forms or validate arguments before invocation.

Retrieve the current status and result of a background job by its identifier. Requires an authenticated user with the `admin` scope. Returns the job `id`, a short `status` (for example `queued`, `running`, `finished`, `failed`, or `cancelled`), and an optional `result` payload when available. Use this endpoint to poll job progress after creating a job.

delete.description: Request cancellation of a background job. Requires `admin` scope. This endpoint performs a best-effort cancel: if the job is `queued` or `running` it will be marked `cancelled`. Returns 204 No Content.

post.description: Create a background job request. Accepts a `JobRequest` with a `type` and an optional `payload`. Returns HTTP 202 Accepted with a `Location` header pointing to `/v1/jobs/{job_id}` where callers can poll status. This endpoint supports an `Idempotency-Key` header: if the same key is used, the server will return the same job id (24h dedup). Requires `admin` scope.

get.description: Open a Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream to receive real-time job progress events for the given `job_id`. Clients should keep the connection open to receive status updates such as `running`, `finished`, or custom progress events emitted by workers. This demo will subscribe to Redis Pub/Sub if available or emit a single current-status event as a fallback. In production, use a persistent event source (Redis, message bus) for live streaming.

Return a paginated list of available models exposed by the platform. The list is discovered from LLM adapters when present and falls back to a deterministic demo model when adapters are missing. Each item contains model metadata such as name, provider, context window, supported modalities, and a short description. The endpoint supports `ETag` conditional requests and pagination via `page_size` and `page_token`.

post.description: Request a single-turn text completion from the configured model. Provide a `prompt` and optional `model`, `temperature`, and `max_tokens`. If `model` is omitted the server will use a configured default. The response contains the completed text, token usage (when the adapter reports it), latency, and provenance identifiers. Authentication is required. This endpoint is suitable for quick, synchronous completions.

Compute vector embeddings for the provided input text. POST an `EmbeddingRequest` with the `input` string and optional `model` to compute an embedding vector. The response contains an array of embedding objects (each with an `embedding` vector and `model` field). If embedding adapters are unavailable a demo empty vector is returned.

Multi-turn chat completion endpoint. POST a `ChatRequest` containing an ordered list of `messages` (each message is an object with `role` and `content`) and an optional `model`. The adapter may return a streaming response or a structured chat response; in this lightweight API we return a single JSON payload with one or more choices. If the chat adapter is not available a demo assistant reply is returned.

get.description:
Return the available model instances and lightweight metadata used by the platform and clients.

This endpoint returns an array of model descriptors (name, provider, modalities, whether the
instance is loaded and the currently selected default). The response may come from the
platform's runtime adapter when available or fall back to a demo/default entry when the
adapter is not present. Authentication is required; non-admin users may call this to discover
what models exist and which is marked as default.

Notes:
- Response shape: list of ModelInfo objects.
- This endpoint is read-only and safe to call frequently (clients may cache results).

schema.title: Response List Instances V1 Admin Models Instances Get

post.description:
Load or prepare a model instance on the platform runtime.

Admin-only operation that asks the runtime adapter to load or stage a model instance so it
is available for low-latency use. The request accepts `modelKey` (or `name`) and optional
adapter-specific `options`. The endpoint returns a small object containing an `id` that can
be used to reference the instance in subsequent admin calls. On systems without a runtime
adapter this endpoint returns a demo/compatibility response and does not change runtime
behavior.

schema.title: Response Create Instance V1 Admin Models Instances Post

get.description:
Return the current default model name used by the platform.

This endpoint resolves the platform-wide default model (or the configured fallback). Clients
can call this to determine which model name will be used when no explicit model is provided.
Authentication is required. The response is a simple JSON object with a single `name` field.

schema.title: Response Get Defaults V1 Admin Models Defaults Get

patch.description:
Change the platform default model selection.

Admin-only endpoint. Clients should supply the canonical model name to be marked as the
platform default. On platforms with a pluggable adapter this will attempt to call the
adapter to persist the selection; when the adapter is missing this call may succeed only in
the local/demo sense (no runtime change). Returns an ActionResponse with `ok` and a
human-readable `message` describing the outcome.

delete.description:
Unload or free a previously prepared model instance.

Admin-only operation. Requests to this endpoint ask the runtime adapter to unload resources
associated with the provided instance id. On success the endpoint returns HTTP 204 No
Content. If the adapter is unavailable the platform may respond with a demo/no-op success
message; otherwise a 400 error is returned when unloading is not possible.

get.description:
Retrieve details for a specific model instance identified by `instance_id`.

Admin-only read endpoint. Returns the instance record (id, name and any adapter-provided
`details`) if known. Returns 404 when the instance cannot be found. This endpoint is useful
for debugging, instrumenting, or confirming the state of a prepared model instance.

schema.title: Response Get Instance V1 Admin Models Instances  Instance Id  Get

post.summary: Run a short test prompt against an instance
post.description:
Run a short diagnostic prompt against a specific loaded model instance.

This endpoint allows callers (non-admins allowed) to exercise a single quick prompt on the
named instance. The request body accepts an optional `model` override, the `prompt`, and
basic generation parameters such as `temperature` and `max_tokens`. The response contains
the model `output`, token `usage` when available, and provenance fields (`trace_id` and
`event_id`) to correlate diagnostics with platform logs. If the runtime adapter does not
support testing, a demo response will be returned.

get.description:
Return the available built-in model manifests exposed by the platform.

This admin-only endpoint lists manifests that were either bundled with the platform or
previously activated via the builtins manifest staging workflow. Each manifest entry is a
structured document describing a set of curated model definitions, versions, and metadata
that administrators can activate for the runtime. The response is an array of manifest
objects as produced by the registry service.

schema.title: Response List Builtins V1 Admin Models Manifests Builtins Get

post.description:
Fetch and stage a remote builtins manifest for later activation.

Admin-only idempotent operation that downloads and validates a manifest document from a
remote URL and stages it in the registry for review. The staging step does not activate the
manifest for runtime usage; it merely prepares the manifest and records a staged version that
can later be activated. If an `Idempotency-Key` header is supplied repeat calls will return
the same staged result.

Activate the most recently staged builtins manifest.

Admin-only operation that promotes a previously staged manifest to active status. Activation
typically results in registry updates and may alter which built-in models the platform
exposes to users. This action is idempotent when an `Idempotency-Key` header is provided.
If activation fails (validation, conflicts, or adapter errors) the endpoint returns HTTP 400
with error details.

Rollback the active builtins manifest to the previous version.

Admin-only convenience for reverting a recent activation. The service will attempt to
restore the previously active manifest; if no prior version exists or the operation fails a
400 error is returned with details. The response contains the restored version metadata on
success.

get.description:
Return a history of activated builtins manifests.

Admin-only endpoint that queries the platform store for previous manifest activations and
their timestamps. Each entry contains the manifest version, activation timestamp, and the
manifest payload where available. Useful for auditing and diagnosing what manifest versions
were active at particular times.

List configured runtime LLM providers available to the platform.

Admin-only endpoint that returns a paginated list of registered runtime LLM providers. Each
entry includes a provider id and optional metadata (base_url, default model, tenant binding,
etc). Clients can use this to discover which external LLM backends are available for
assignment to tenants or for runtime orchestration.

schema.title: Response List Providers V1 Admin Models Providers Get

post.description:
Register a new runtime LLM provider with the platform.

Admin-only operation to add or register an external LLM endpoint for use by the
orchestrator. The request should include the provider `name`, `base_url`, and optional
fields like `model` and `api_key`. On success the provider will be available for selection
and orchestration.

get.summary: Get resolved main LLM provider for a tenant (or global if none)
get.description:
Get the resolved main LLM provider for a tenant or the global default.

Admin-only helper that returns which runtime LLM provider the platform will use for a
given tenant (or the global default when no tenant_id is supplied). This is useful for
multi-tenant setups to confirm provider resolution logic.

schema.title: Response Get Main Client V1 Admin Models Providers Main Get

get.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific runtime LLM provider.

Admin-only endpoint that returns provider metadata (registration info, base_url, model
binding, and any runtime client configuration). Returns 404 if the provider id is unknown.

schema.title: Response Get Provider V1 Admin Models Providers  Provider Id  Get

patch.description:
Update registration details for an existing runtime LLM provider.

Admin-only operation. Supply any of the optional fields (base_url, model, api_key,
tenant_id) to update the provider registration. The platform will attempt to re-register
the provider with merged settings. Returns an ActionResponse with the provider name on
success.

delete.description:
Unregister and remove a runtime LLM provider from the platform.

Admin-only operation that removes the provider registration. On success the endpoint
returns HTTP 204 No Content. Errors during unregistering are returned as HTTP 400 with
details.

put.summary: Set a provider as default/global (or per-tenant)
put.description:
Set a runtime LLM provider as the global or tenant-scoped default.

Admin-only endpoint that assigns the given provider as the default globally or for a
specified tenant (when `tenant_id` is supplied). This affects provider resolution for
requests that do not explicitly specify a provider. Returns an ActionResponse with the
selected provider name on success.

get.description:
Return active and recently recorded built-in model processes managed by the platform.

This endpoint queries the in-memory/runtime store to list currently running processes
started by the builtins orchestration and also merges persisted audit records from the
platform store when available. Each process entry contains identifiers such as `id`,
`artifact`, `pid`, `port`, and `ts` (timestamp). Admin-level access is typically required to
inspect process metadata.

schema.title: Response List Processes V1 Admin Processes Get

delete.description:
Stop a builtin model process by its operating system pid.

This endpoint attempts to unload the process associated with the provided pid using the
runtime LLM adapter and then removes the runtime metadata from the platform cache to
prevent stale entries. The operation is idempotent and returns 204 when the process is
stopped or when it was already gone.

get.description:
Return a recent activation history of builtins manifests.

This endpoint queries the platform store for previously activated builtins manifests and
returns their versions and activation timestamps. Useful for auditing which manifest
versions have been active over time.

schema.title: Response History Manifests V1 Admin Processes History Manifests Get

get.description:
Return a recent history of builtin process records persisted by the platform.

Admin-oriented audit endpoint that returns previously recorded process lifecycle events and
their metadata (id, artifact, pid, port, timestamp). Useful for troubleshooting and
reconstructing what processes ran when.

schema.title: Response History Processes V1 Admin Processes History Processes Get

get.description:
Return a paginated list of background jobs managed by the platform.

Admin-facing endpoint that returns job identifiers and their current status. The
response is paginated and follows a simple `items` / `next_page_token` shape. This proxy
wraps the demo in-memory job store for local testing; real deployments will map to the
platform's persistent job service.

post.description:
Create a background job via the canonical job creation endpoint.

    Admin proxy that forwards the incoming request body to the canonical job creation
    implementation. This route mirrors `/v1/jobs:create` but is exposed under the admin
    mount so administrative tools can create jobs with the same semantics and authentication
    as normal clients. The response and headers are passed through from the canonical
    handler.

delete.description:
Cancel an existing background job by id (admin proxy).

    Proxy endpoint that delegates cancellation requests to the canonical job cancellation
    handler. Intended for administrative tooling to cancel jobs on behalf of users or to
    perform emergency cleanup. Returns the canonical handler's response.

get.description:
Return a paginated list of tenants registered in the platform.

Admin-only endpoint that enumerates tenant records. The response is paginated and may be
ETagged for caching. Each tenant includes basic metadata such as id, name, admin_email and
free-form `metadata` useful for tenant-scoped configuration.

schema.title: Response List Tenants V1 Admin Tenants Get

post.description:
Create a new tenant record.

Admin-only operation that provisions a tenant id and basic tenant metadata. For auditing the
request must include the `X-Tenant-Id` header indicating which administrative tenant or
context initiated the creation. Returns the created Tenant object on success.

get.description:
Retrieve a tenant by its id.

Admin-only read endpoint that returns the tenant record for the requested `tenant_id`.
Returns HTTP 404 when the tenant cannot be found.

patch.description:
Update tenant metadata or administrative contact information.

Admin-only operation that applies a partial update to the tenant record. Supply only the
fields to change in the request body (name, admin_email, metadata). Returns the updated
tenant record on success.

delete.description:
Delete a tenant from the platform.

Admin-only destructive operation that removes the tenant record and any associated
tenant-scoped configuration. Use with caution — callers should ensure dependent resources
are cleaned up first. Returns a simple `{ "ok": true }` on success.

schema.title: Response Delete Tenant V1 Admin Tenants  Tenant Id  Delete

post.description:
Set a short-lived UI override that influences the builtins auto-start decision.

Internal endpoint used by the UI to request that the platform temporarily allow or
disallow automatic startup of staged built-in model processes. This call is only honored
when the operator has enabled UI overrides via configuration; otherwise it returns an
indication that the override is not allowed. The payload should include `enable: true|false`.

schema.title: Response Set Auto Start Override V1 Internal Ops Auto Start Override Post

get.description:
Preview staged builtins manifests and provide estimated resource footprint and auto-start recommendations.

Internal diagnostic endpoint used by operator/UIs to see which staged builtins would be allowed
to auto-start given current system heuristics (memory, whitelist, concurrency limits, and UI
override). This does not perform activation; it only returns annotated entries for inspection.

schema.title: Response Preview Staged V1 Internal Ops Preview Staged Get
